requirement:
When authoring evidence for a named example, its complete fenced declaration
MUST be included in the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`.
rationale:
The subject has one obligation. When evidence is authored for a named example, the example's complete fenced declaration MUST be in the mandatory input set. `requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` is cited as context, so I did not reassess it. Two marked tests cover the obligation.

- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors]` is marked `{test}` for the subject. It declares `:::{example} case` in the project and calls `AssessmentSources::prepare(root, "requirements.case")`.
  - It asserts that `subject_kind` is `Definition(Example, false)`.
  - It asserts that `mandatory_inputs()[0]["requirements"]` is `requirements.case`.
  - It asserts that `mandatory_inputs()[0]["text"]` equals the exact array: the opening fence `:::{example} case`, the body line, and the closing `:::`. This is a strict check that the whole fenced declaration is included.
  - The same test also checks the example when it is a cited input of another subject. The bundle for `requirements.ready` must contain an input whose `requirements` is `requirements.case`.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[citation_metadata_is_hidden_in_fenced_sections_and_preserved_in_details]` is also marked `{test}`. For the `:::{example} case` variant, it calls `AssessmentSources::prepare` on `guide.case`. It asserts that `subject_text` contains the citation metadata lines, and that some mandatory input's joined text contains them. The declaration's body is therefore included unredacted, even though the book rendering hides it.

I found no failure case or boundary that the text names for this obligation. Plausible violations would be a missing example input, an input that is only a body excerpt, or one without the fence lines. The exact-text assertion would reject all three. Deduplication, ordering and exclusions belong to `requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` and are outside this subject. I found no gap.
